subject: Reasoning
description: Circular-seating puzzles, facing centre vs outwards, deductions

questions.stem: Six friends A, B, C, D, E, F sit around a circular table FACING THE CENTRE. A is between F and C. B is opposite to A. D is to the left of B. E is to the right of B. Who is to the IMMEDIATE LEFT of A?

options.option_text: F is to A's immediate left
C is to A's immediate left
D is to A's immediate left
E is to A's immediate left

questions.explanation: Six positions, facing centre. Place A. B is OPPOSITE A. D is left of B (so D is on B's left → from centre, D is to viewer's right of B); E is right of B. A is between F + C → F + C flank A. Now from A's perspective (facing centre): A's left is one neighbour, right is other. Working through: when facing centre, my LEFT = clockwise. With A at top, B at bottom: C to A's clockwise (left) = C to A's left; F to A's right. Distractors are wrong configurations.

questions.stem: Five people P, Q, R, S, T sit around a round table FACING THE CENTRE. Q is to the right of P. R is opposite P. S is between R and T. Who is opposite Q?

options.option_text: S is opposite Q here
T is opposite Q here
R is opposite Q here
P is opposite Q here

questions.explanation: 5 positions = irregular pentagon, no exact 'opposite' but for analytical purposes: place P at 12 o'clock; Q on P's right (clockwise → 4 o'clock); R opposite to P (≈ 6 o'clock). S is between R + T. Remaining slots ≈ 8 o'clock + 10 o'clock for S, T. With S between R + T, layout: P (12), Q (~4-5), R (~6-7), S (~8-9), T (~10-11). Across from Q (at 4) ≈ T (at 10). So T 'opposite' Q. ✓

questions.stem: 8 people sit equally spaced around a circular table, FACING THE CENTRE. If A is exactly opposite B, B is exactly opposite A. How many seats are between A and B in one direction?

options.option_text: 2 seats are between A and B
3 seats are between A and B
4 seats are between A and B
1 seat is between A and B

questions.explanation: 8 seats around circle. Opposite seats are 4 positions apart (180°). So A + B at positions 1 + 5 (say). Between them in one direction: positions 2, 3, 4 = 3 seats. (In other direction: positions 6, 7, 8 = 3 seats too.) Distractor 4 = total positions including B. Distractor 2 = wrong count.

questions.stem: Six persons sit around circle facing OUTSIDE. From centre's view, when an outward-facing person turns 'to his RIGHT', it is which clockwise direction?

options.option_text: Their left is clockwise from outside view
Their right is anticlockwise from outside
It is same direction as facing-inward case
There is no fixed convention possible

questions.explanation: When FACING CENTRE: their right = clockwise. When FACING OUT: their right = anticlockwise (mirror reverses left/right relative to fixed observer). This direction inversion catches students. ALWAYS confirm facing direction at the start of each problem!

questions.stem: Five persons V, W, X, Y, Z around a round table facing CENTRE. V is between W and X. Y is to the immediate right of W. Z is to the immediate left of X. Who is sitting opposite V (approx)?

options.option_text: Y is exactly opposite V here always
Y or Z (5-seat table = no exact opposite)
W is exactly opposite V approximately
X is exactly opposite V approximately

questions.explanation: 5 seats — no exact opposite. Layout (facing centre, going clockwise): say V at 12. W on V's left (~9-10 area), X on V's right (~2-3 area). Y immediate right of W → Y at ~7-8. Z immediate left of X → Z at ~4-5. So opposite-ish to V (12 o'clock) lies between Y (7-8) + Z (4-5) — i.e., near 6 o'clock. Both Y + Z are 'across' from V; with 5 seats, no exact opposite.

questions.stem: If A, B, C, D, E, F sit at a hexagonal table (6 seats) facing CENTRE, and A is opposite D, then immediate neighbours of A's opposite (D) are:

options.option_text: A and D themselves are neighbours always
Two of B, C, E, F (the seat-2 neighbours)
Just one neighbour beside D's chair
Three neighbours flanking D's seat here

questions.explanation: 6 seats around hexagonal table. D has 2 immediate neighbours (one on each side). With A opposite to D (3 seats apart on each side), the 4 seats between are B, C, E, F — D's neighbours are 2 of these (the ones immediately flanking D). Without further info, we can't say which two; but ANY two from B, C, E, F (specifically the seats immediately to D's left + right). Distractor 1 — A is opposite, not adjacent.

questions.stem: Eight people sit around a circular table facing CENTRE. A is to immediate right of B; C is opposite A; D is to immediate left of C. The seat directly opposite D is occupied by:

options.option_text: A himself is opposite D here
B is exactly opposite D here
C is exactly opposite D here
Cannot be determined from clues

questions.explanation: 8 seats; opposite = 4 seats apart. Place A at position 1; B at position 2 (since A is right of B = A at clockwise from B; facing centre 'right' = clockwise, so A is at B's right means A is one CW step from B → B at position 8 or A at position 1 + B at position 2 if reverse. Take simpler: B at 2, A at 1 (so A is to immediate right of B from B's view is anticlockwise = position 1 if B at 2, facing centre — so working). C opposite A → C at position 5. D immediate left of C → D at position 6 (from C facing centre, left = CW = position 6). Opposite D (6) is position 2 = B. ✓
